Under public utility contracts (such as central power grids, railway signaling specifications, and state electricity boards), paper-insulated copper or aluminum cables must carry certified lab records showing that the ash content of the paper does not exceed specified limits to legally enter commercial distribution.
requirements: Observed or calculated final ash content percentages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 to match the significant places of the specified values.
Any inorganic impurity in insulating paper tends to reduce its dielectric property, which can lead to localized electrical tracking and cable breakdown under high voltages.
The test specimen must consist of a raw insulating paper sample weighing at least 1 g.

Before ignition, the paper specimen must be dried to constant mass at a temperature of 100°C to 105°C to eliminate environmental humidity, reweighed to an accuracy of 0.1 mg inside the ignited crucible.
The reweighed conditioned sample is placed inside a platinum, fused aluminum, silica, or porcelain crucible and ignited in a muffle furnace or by a gas burner, raising the temperature to 900 ± 25°C.
To avoid the loss of lightweight ash particles during initial heating, the crucible lid must be fully in place during the initial charring stage.
When peak ignition temperature is attained, the lid must be slid slightly to one side to admit oxygen for complete carbon combustion, ensuring draft protection.
When the paper is completely burnt (indicated by the absolute absence of black carbon particles), the crucible with its lid on is cooled to ambient room temperature in a desiccator.
The crucible is weighed to the nearest 0.1 mg, and the ignition, cooling, and weighing cycle is repeated sequentially until the mass remains constant.

The percentage of inorganic ash content is calculated dry-on-dry using the formula: Ash Content, % = [(W3 - W2) / W1] * 100, where W1 is sample weight, W2 is empty crucible weight, and W3 is crucible plus ash weight.

Defines direct interaction as the interaction between simultaneously applied factors of influence that differs fundamentally from that occurring when those same factors are applied sequentially.
Defines indirect interaction as the interaction between simultaneously applied factors of influence that remains essentially unchanged when those same factors are applied sequentially.
Single-factor testing is technically valid and preferred only when interactions between service stress factors are absent or unknown.

Sequential procedures may be developed in which alternative consequential actions are listed to cover each possible outcome of a preceding action.

Where service relationships and aging interactions are not confidently known, technical committees or manufacturers must instigate research to identify specific aging factors, their relative importance, and their physical interactions.

requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, gassing rates (in mm³/min), or gas volumes must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The gassing cell must be subjected to a stable, sinusoidal high-voltage potential of 12 kV at power frequency (50 Hz or 60 Hz) to initiate localized ionization at the gas-liquid interface.
The entire gassing cell assembly must be immersed in a thermostatically controlled oil/liquid bath maintained at a stable temperature of 80 ± 0.5°C throughout the test duration.
The gas phase inside the cell must consist of high-purity nitrogen gas, which is bubbled through the liquid sample prior to the test to achieve complete gas saturation.

Due to the slow kinetics of gas evolution/absorption under nitrogen, the test must be maintained continuously for 18 hours (for 50 Hz systems) or 15 hours (for 60 Hz systems) to obtain a representative cumulative gassing rate.
Results are reported as the net change in gas volume (in mm³) or as a normalized gassing rate (in mm³/min) calculated from pressure changes or burette liquid level movement.
To ensure statistical validity, the gassing test must be performed on at least duplicate specimens, and their results must satisfy standard repeatability criteria.

Duplicate test runs are considered suspect and must be repeated if their calculated gassing tendencies differ by more than a specified repeatability threshold (typically 0.3 + 0.26·|G| mm³/min, where G is the mean gassing value).

To prevent cross-contamination and solvent residue staining, the borosilicate glass cell and electrodes must be thoroughly cleaned with n-heptane, petroleum ether, or 1,1,1-trichloroethane and dried completely before refilling.

Because the test involves a combination of high-voltage ionization (12 kV), heated flammable oils (80°C), and pressurized gases, a secure, transparent safety shield must be installed around the gassing cell to protect laboratory operators.

standard.description: This standard specifies requirements for single-core and multicore halogen-free, flame-retardant, low-smoke (HFFR) insulated and sheathed (if any) electrical cables/cords with rigid or flexible conductors. These cables are designed for use in power and lighting installations in AC single-phase or three-phase systems operating at rated voltages up to and including 1 100 V (1.1 kV) a.c. (50 Hz) or DC systems up to and including 1 500 V to earth.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Electrical Cables (Quality Control) Order' (Cables QCO 2020) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Halogen-Free Flame Retardant (HFFR) cables manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17048 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or selling uncertified HFFR cables is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial electrotechnical cables, as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Every cable reel or attached label must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Conductors must be composed of high-purity annealed bare or tinned copper or aluminium complying with Class 2 (stranded) or Class 5 (flexible) of IS 8130.

Cables are insulated with halogen-free flame-retardant (HFFR) compounds, designated based on material type and rated conductor temperature: a) HFI-TP 70: Thermoplastic HFFR, 70°C maximum; b) HFI-TP 90: Thermoplastic HFFR, 90°C maximum; c) HFI-XL 70: Crosslinked (thermosetting) HFFR, 70°C; d) HFI-XL 90: Crosslinked (thermosetting) HFFR, 90°C.

Sheathing (if any) must be composed of HFFR compounds designated as: a) HFS-TP 70: Thermoplastic HFFR sheathing, 70°C [1]; b) HFS-TP 90: Thermoplastic HFFR sheathing, 90°C [1]; c) HFS-XL 70: Crosslinked HFFR sheathing, 70°C [1]; d) HFS-XL 90: Crosslinked HFFR sheathing, 90°C [1]. Properties after air oven aging are tested as per Amendment No. 1 (80°C for HFS-TP 70 and 100°C for others) [1].

To ensure safety of life and prevent equipment corrosion in fires, cables must meet strict low-smoke and non-toxic emission boundaries: a) Halogen acid gas evolution (measured as HCl) must not exceed a maximum of 0.5 percent by weight; b) Smoke emission must have a minimum of 70 percent light transmittance (negligible smoke opacity); c) Evolved gases must have a pH of minimum 4.3 and a maximum electrical conductivity of 10 µS/mm.

Finished cables must be self-extinguishing and pass mandatory flame tests under IS 10810: a) Flame retardance on single cable (Part 61); b) Flame retardance on bunched cables (Part 62) to prevent rapid fire spread in vertical cable trays.
Insulation and sheathing must undergo tensile strength, elongation at break, hot set, cold bend, and air oven aging tests to ensure long-term physical durability.

However, under the mandatory quality control orders (QCO) for electric ceiling, table, and pedestal fans, the auxiliary motor capacitors are legally required to carry the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped or embossed on their containers to certify safety and quality compliance.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, capacitance percentages, and test voltages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Capacitor elements are built using high-purity, double-sided aluminum-zinc metallized polypropylene film inside a dry plastic or aluminum container, which is manufactured under dust-controlled, air-conditioned conditions to prevent particulate tracking.

When a localized dielectric breakdown occurs at a weak point in the film, the metallized layer evaporates within 5 to 10 microseconds, extinguishing the arc and instantly restoring the insulation level to its full value.
Standardizes preferred microfarad ratings (1.0 to 10.0 μF), including common domestic sizes: 2.00, 2.25, 2.50, 3.15, and 4.00 μF with standard tolerances restricted to ± 5%.
Designed to operate continuously without thermal runaway or accelerated capacitance droppage across a temperature range of -25°C to +85°C.
The tangent of the loss angle (tan δ) or power factor of the capacitor must not exceed 0.002 (or 0.2%) at rated frequency to prevent localized internal heat generation.
Insulation resistance evaluated under 500 V DC between the terminals and the outer metal container must exceed specified minimum thresholds (typically 3000 seconds) to guarantee user safety.
Under active Amendment No. 3 (June 2020), Clause 7.3.2 (Insulation Resistance between terminals) is completely deleted to streamline dielectric testing and avoid redundant metrics.
Completed capacitors must withstand a sinusoidal AC test potential of 1.5 times the rated voltage between terminals for 10 seconds without dielectric puncture.
To ensure absolute user protection from electric shock, capacitors must withstand 2000 V AC applied between the shorted terminals and the container for 10 seconds without breakdown.
Capacitors must survive continuous heating at +85°C under an overvoltage of 1.25 times the rated voltage for a minimum of 500 hours, with a maximum capacitance droppage of less than 3% to 5%.

standard.description: This Indian Standard unifies the technical recommendations, design criteria, constructional guides, and performance requirements for the planning, design, and maintenance of lighting installations in library buildings. It covers both artificial lighting and natural daylighting to ensure sufficient illumination quantity and quality for diverse reading and archiving tasks, minimizing eyestrain during long periods of work.

However, under state public library guidelines, central university library layouts, and central public works department (CPWD) technical specifications, newly built library systems are legally audited and designed to conform with the illumination and glare levels specified under IS 2672.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, lux measurements, daylight factors, and reflection percentages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The light given by a source, or received by a surface, or transmitted by a medium, irrespective of the way in which it is distributed spatially as regards direction. Measured in lumens (lm).
The luminous flux emitted within unit solid angle (one steradian) by a point source having a uniform intensity of one candela.

The unit of luminous intensity. Magnitude is defined as one-sixtieth of the luminous intensity of one square centimetre of a black-body radiator operated at the temperature of solidification of platinum.
The reading desks and study areas must maintain a stable horizontal illumination level of 150 to 300 lux to allow continuous reading without eyestrain.
To ensure book titles are clearly legible, a vertical illumination level of 50 to 100 lux must be maintained across the vertical spines of books stored on stacks and shelves.
The ceiling surface must have a reflection factor of 70% to 80% (using matte white or off-white paint) to maximize indirect diffuse reflection.
The walls must maintain a reflection factor of 50% to 60% with light-coloured, matte finishes.
Reading tables and desks must have a reflection factor of 30% to 40% to reduce contrast between white paper pages and table surfaces, minimizing eyestrain.
Study and reading rooms are highly encouraged to utilize natural daylighting, maintaining a minimum Daylight Factor of 1.5% across study zones.
To maintain visual comfort and prevent veiling reflections on glossy paper pages, the direct Glare Index inside reading rooms must be restricted to a maximum of 19.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Electrical Cables (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Government of India, all Crosslinked Polyethylene Insulated Thermoplastic Sheathed Cables for working voltages up to 1 100 Volts must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, selling, or importing uncertified cables is a criminal offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial electrotechnical cables, as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Every cable drum or attached label must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Conductors must be composed of plain copper or aluminium wires complying with IS 8130. For gassy mines, mining cables must feature copper conductors exclusively (tinned copper allowed on agreement).

The extruded cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation must comply with strict physical-chemical limits: a) Tensile strength must be minimum 12.5 N/mm²; b) Elongation at break must be minimum 200 percent; c) After air oven aging (135 ± 3 °C for 7 days), maximum variation in tensile strength and elongation must not exceed ±25 percent; d) Hot set test (200 ± 3 °C, 15 min under 20 N/cm² load) must yield maximum elongation under load of 175% and maximum permanent elongation after cooling of 15%; e) Shrinkage test (130 ± 3 °C for 1 h) must not exceed 4.0%; f) Gravimetric water absorption (85 ± 2 °C for 14 days) must be maximum 1 mg/cm²; g) Volume resistivity must be minimum 1 x 10^14 ohm-cm at 27 °C and 1 x 10^12 ohm-cm at 90 °C.

The polyethylene (PE) sheathing compound must satisfy: a) Tensile strength min 12.5 N/mm² and elongation min 300% before aging; b) Air oven aging (110 ± 2 °C for 7 days) must yield minimum elongation of 300%; c) Hot deformation test (110 ± 2 °C for 6 h) must have a maximum indentation depth of 50 percent; d) Carbon black content for black sheaths must be 2.5 ± 0.5 percent.

Low Smoke Halogen Free (LSHF) sheathing (Type ST8 and ST12) must satisfy: a) Type ST8 tensile strength min 9.0 N/mm² and elongation min 125%; Type ST12 tensile strength min 12.5 N/mm² and elongation min 300%; b) Oven aging (ST8: 100 ± 2 °C for 7 days, max variation ±40%; ST12: 110 ± 2 °C for 10 days, max variation ±30%); c) Hot deformation (ST8: 80 ± 2 °C for 4 h, max indentation 50%; ST12: 110 ± 2 °C for 4 h, max indentation 50%); d) Cold elongation and cold impact test must show zero cracks and min 20% elongation at -15 ± 2 °C for 3 h; e) Shrinkage test (80 ± 2 °C for 5 h) must be maximum 3 percent.

Armour must consist of galvanized round steel wires, formed steel wires (strips), or non-magnetic elements applied with a minimum coverage of 90 percent, calculated using the formula: Percent coverage = (N * d / W) * 100, where W = π * D * Cos α. The direction of lay of the armour must be left-hand.

Cables must be designated using standard letters: Aluminium conductor = A (no code letter for copper); XLPE insulation = 2X; Steel round wire armour = W; Non-magnetic round wire armour = Wa; Steel strip armour = F; Non-magnetic strip armour = Fa; Double steel strip armour = FF; Double steel round wire armour = WW; PVC outer sheath = Y; PE outer sheath = 2Y; LSHF outer sheath = Z.

Cables designed for fire-retardancy (Categories C1, C2, and C3) must satisfy: a) Flammability burning period must not exceed 60 s; b) Oxygen Index must be minimum 29; c) Temperature Index must be minimum 250 °C; d) Smoke density rating must be maximum 60 (FR-LSH) or 20 (LSHF); e) Halogen acid gas evolution (HCl) must be maximum 20% (FR-LSH) or 0.5% (LSHF); f) Light transmission for LSHF must be minimum 70 percent; g) Evolved gases must have a pH of minimum 4.3 and conductivity of maximum 10 µS/mm.

Drums must be selected randomly based on lot size: up to 25 drums (select 3, permissible defectives = 0); 26-50 (select 5, permissible defectives = 0); 51-100 (select 8, permissible defectives = 0); 101-300 (select 13, permissible defectives = 1); 301-500 (select 20, permissible defectives = 1); 501 and above (select 32, permissible defectives = 2). A drum sample is marked 'defective' if it fails any acceptance test.
